title: Touring with Buddy Petit to Mobile, Montgomery and small towns
summary: Weeks with Buddy Petit in Mobile and Montgomery parks and one-night stands in small Alabama towns.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters

blocks.x: No, I don't remember when he came there but I remember Punch Miller already. I didn't know where he came there. When did you first hear Joe Oliver? First time I heard Joe Oliver was in Pensacola when he came there I think it was. Yeah. Where did he play? He played at the hall there. Coyle Street Hall where I played at. What's the name of it? Coyle Street Hall. Call it Coyle Street. I forgot a map of Pensacola and I forgot what it looks like. Coyle Street Hall and then they had one on the Bella Street Hall, two halls. Then they had their parks right off the water, all open, everything open at me, to build the Pistler Park. You were telling me on the way, on the streetcar coming up I guess, I remember we were walking, Canal Street, about Mobile. Yeah, Mobile, Alabama. I played with Buddy Petit in Mobile. We left Pensacola and went to Mobile and played there. We played there for a week for a school teacher. I'm trying to think of her name, what was that one the name? But anyway she hired us to play there and we played there a week at this park in Mobile, Alabama. And I was staying on Conception Street there, down the bay they call it, Mobile. So we played there and then when we left there we went on back to Pensacola. And we played there in Pensacola I think for another week because we went to Montgomery and played. Washington Park in Montgomery, Alabama. So when we left Montgomery we went back to Pensacola and then Buddy Petit and him, I think we played one night there, one night and then they got ready to leave the next day to come back to New Orleans.
